prompt:
Return only a complete Python module that implements the request.
Do not use Markdown fences. Do not include commentary outside the Python source.
Use the supplied plan as the implementation specification. The safety document is not available in this context.

Implementation request:
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

Plan:
SOURCE: url supplied by the caller, the hostnames it names, and every redirect Location returned by transport
TRUST: untrusted; the URL or a redirect target may use a disallowed scheme or port, embed credentials, or name a host that resolves to a non-public address
SINK: calling transport to make an outbound HTTP request
GUARD: require a hostname, no username or password, and either HTTP with an omitted port or port 80, or HTTPS with an omitted port or port 443, otherwise raise ValueError; resolve the hostname with resolve_host and raise ValueError if it yields no addresses or any address is not a global public address; on a redirect response read the Location header case-insensitively, raise ValueError if it is missing, resolve it against the current URL, and apply this same complete validation to the new destination before requesting it; follow at most five redirects and raise ValueError when a sixth would be needed
ORDER: validate every destination before each transport call
EFFECT: return the response body of the first 200 status reached through validated hops only
END_PLAN
